beats.narration_slice: In 1935, Erwin Schrödinger imagined a cat sealed in a box.
beats.visual: Surreal cut-paper portrait of 1930s physicist Erwin Schrödinger at a small desk, looking toward a recessed cardboard shadow-box containing the silhouette of a calm cat behind a firmly closed wooden lid, with warm barn-umber outer layers fading into indigo interior shadow.
beats.purpose: show Schrödinger conceiving the sealed-cat thought experiment
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium-wide three-quarter view; seated 1930s physicist beside a closed cat shadow-box; desk-level composition; warm cream and umber foreground against a deep indigo recessed compartment
beats.continuity: moves from the barn-book transition into a conceptual 1930s physics scene while preserving the same layered cardboard shadow-box grammar

beats.narration_slice: Inside, a radioactive atom may decay or not.
beats.visual: Extreme close view inside the sealed-box world: a simplified graphite-drawn radioactive atom motif floats above an early-20th-century detector, while two translucent torn-paper probability traces diverge around it to suggest decay and non-decay without labels.
beats.purpose: show the atom having two possible outcomes
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme close-up; atom motif centered above vintage detector hardware; two diverging cyan-green probability traces; dark indigo interior with no cat visible
beats.continuity: dives through the closed box from the previous exterior conception into its unseen internal atomic setup

beats.narration_slice: Decay triggers a mechanism that releases poison.
beats.visual: Side-on technical cut-paper view of a plausible 1930s detector-and-lever apparatus in motion: a triggered relay pulls a mechanical linkage that tips a small stoppered poison vessel, shown abstractly and without any animal in frame.
beats.purpose: show the causal chain from atomic decay to the poison-release mechanism
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight side profile; activated relay, descending lever and tipped glass vessel forming a diagonal cause-and-effect chain; graphite machinery against smoky cardboard layers
beats.continuity: follows the atomic possibility into the specific mechanical consequence using the same box interior

beats.narration_slice: No decay means the cat survives.
beats.visual: Low-angle interior view of the box with a calm alert cat sitting upright in a warm pool of cream light; behind it, the detector and lever remain visibly motionless and the poison vessel stays securely upright.
beats.purpose: show that without decay the mechanism does not fire and the cat remains alive
beats.visual_fingerprint: low-angle medium shot; living cat upright in foreground; dormant mechanism receding behind it; warm ochre illumination replacing the prior mechanical close-up
beats.continuity: contrasts the triggered mechanism with its alternate inactive state inside the same conceptual box

beats.narration_slice: Quantum theory allows both atomic possibilities in superposition.
beats.visual: Abstract overhead collage where two translucent versions of the atom occupy the same central space, one surrounded by a decay-like burst and the other by an intact orbital form, interwoven with restrained wave-like cyan-green traces over layered indigo paper.
beats.purpose: show both atomic possibilities coexisting in superposition
beats.visual_fingerprint: overhead abstract composition; overlapping dual atom states at center; concentric interference waves and torn-paper probability layers; no cat or machinery visible
beats.continuity: pulls away from the literal box interior into a more abstract quantum representation of the two alternatives

beats.narration_slice: That links the cat to both possible fates.
beats.visual: Frontal shadow-box composition in which one cat silhouette overlaps two spatially offset states within the same recessed chamber: an upright alert form in warm paper and a quiet recumbent form in smoky indigo, connected back to the dual atom motif by a single branching graphite-and-cyan linkage.
beats.purpose: show the cat becoming entangled with both possible outcomes
beats.visual_fingerprint: frontal medium-wide view; overlapping upright and recumbent cat silhouettes; branching atomic linkage descending from upper corner; warm-versus-indigo state overlap in one chamber
beats.continuity: translates the abstract atomic superposition from the previous beat into the cat's paired conceptual fates

beats.narration_slice: Schrödinger used this absurd scenario to expose the measurement problem.
beats.visual: Wide surreal shadow-box scene with Schrödinger standing outside the sealed box, one hand near but not touching its latch, while the box interior remains layered with overlapping cat-state silhouettes that collapse toward a single crisp outline only at the edge of the unopened door.
beats.purpose: show that the absurd cat scenario highlights the unresolved role of observation and measurement
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide straight-on composition; physicist outside box at left, untouched latch centered, ambiguous layered cat forms deep inside at right; sharp-to-soft boundary concentrated around the closed door
beats.continuity: returns from the cat's overlapping fates to Schrödinger and the unopened box, framing the ambiguity as the point of the thought experiment
